# Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Context / Problem

Status mapping is hardcoded: outbound reads built-in `local_to_jira_status` at the CREATE/UPDATE
sites; inbound inverts built-in `jira_to_local_status`, preferring a `rebar-status:<local>` label
hardcoded to `blocked`/`cancelled`. A project needing a remap/collapse has no echo-safe path.
Make status config-driven on the S1 core: **map-or-drift** (never coerce); remap/collapse
round-trips via `rebar-status:`.

## Dependency (prerequisite ticket)

On the S1 mapping core **[rebar:bfe7-0900-c3d1-4141]** (merged): `mapping_config` provides
`load_mapping_config(root=None)` + `resolve_for_project(config, key, *, builtin) -> MappingLayer`
(merges `builtin ← default ← projects.<KEY>`) with `.status_map` (local→Jira; `SKIP`=drop,
ABSENT=drift). `local_to_jira_status` is the `builtin`, so no `[mapping]` ⇒ effective map =
today's default — parity unchanged.

## Approach — one FORWARD seam; inbound stays reverse-map-free

Only **outbound (forward)** becomes per-project; inbound needs no reverse map/project key — the
`rebar-status:` label makes every non-built-in status self-describing (4).

1. **`config.py` — forward resolution entry point.** Add
   `effective_status_map(project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` = `load_mapping_config` +
   `resolve_for_project(builtin=LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA)`. The literal stays the built-in fallback
   (parity-tested); `mapping_config` imported LAZILY (config.py stays stdlib-only). No reverse
   resolution.

2. **Outbound consumers read the resolved map via the `OutboundMapper` Protocol.**
   `outbound_differ` resolves the project key once per ticket (`projects_store.resolve_project`
   already runs) and passes the effective `status_map` (optional; `None`→built-in) into both
   Protocol methods: `map_local_to_remote` (CREATE, differ:543) and, via `compute_update_fields`
   (`outbound_field_diff`:291), `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE). The `_backend.py` Protocol
   signatures + the two wrappers (`jira/backend`, `jira_datacenter/backend`) gain the param.
   `.get()` sites reached: `outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE, Cloud+DC),
   `outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields` (Cloud CREATE), `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (DC
   CREATE). `acli.transition_issue` is NOT threaded (gets the ALREADY-mapped name).

3. **Drift = leave Jira as-is, never a per-mutation failure.** Decided ONLY in the mapper: with
   no entry for a local status it **omits the `status` field** (Jira unchanged) + a drift alert,
   replacing today's `.get(status,"To Do")` coerce. `reconcile_helpers.preflight_status_mapping`
   runs AFTER the mapper (`reconcile.py:485`); a drifted mutation carries no `status` field (so is
   non-offending), but a config REMAP makes the mapper emit a config-only Jira NAME absent from
   the BUILT-IN keys∪values it tolerates → spurious warning.
   Widen its tolerated set to built-in keys∪values ∪ a **NEW S2** helper
   `mapping_config.declared_status_names` (thread `repo_root` from `reconcile.py:485`), mirroring
   step 5's fetcher fix; kill-switch untouched.

4. **Generalised `rebar-status:` round-trip (built-in-reverse stamp rule).** Outbound
   (`outbound_labels`): stamp `rebar-status:<local>` **iff
   `config.jira_to_local_status.get(status_map[local]) != local`** (`.get`, no KeyError). On the
   built-in map this selects exactly {blocked, cancelled} (in_progress/closed are canonical
   preimages; `deleted` excluded via `excluded_statuses`) — default stamping preserved. Under ANY
   config remap/collapse, every status whose Jira target isn't the built-in canonical name for
   `<local>` is labelled → inbound recovers it from the label, no reverse map; a DRIFTED status
   has no target → no label. Inbound: parse the `rebar-status:<local>` suffix, validating
   `<local>` against the local-status vocabulary (a constant) via one shared helper; the plain
   `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get()` built-in fallback stays correct since every non-built-in status
   is labelled. Malformed `[mapping]` fails closed via S1's `MappingConfigError`.

5. **Fetcher known-set widened.** `fetcher._known_jira_statuses` today reads only built-in
   `jira_to_local_status` keys → a config-only status trips a spurious "no reconciler mapping"
   warning. Widen to built-in ∪ every Jira NAME declared across config (`status_map` values +
   `statuses`, from `repo_root`) via the same **NEW S2** `mapping_config.declared_status_names`
   helper (Scope below); kill-switch kept.

## Scope (files)

- `config.py` — `effective_status_map` (forward only, lazy `mapping_config`).
- `outbound_differ.py` — resolve project key once; pass `status_map` to CREATE/UPDATE + label diff.
- `outbound_field_diff.py` — `compute_update_fields` forwards `status_map`.
- `_backend.py` — `OutboundMapper` Protocol: optional `status_map` on both map methods.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — wrappers forward `status_map`; DC `_map_local_to_dc_fields` uses it (DC CREATE) w/ drift-omit.
- `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py` — `map_fields_to_remote` uses `status_map` (UPDATE); drift-omit.
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` uses `status_map` (Cloud CREATE); drift-omit.
- `outbound_labels.py` — stamp rule keyed on built-in `config.jira_to_local_status`.
- `inbound_fields.py` — generalised `rebar-status:<local>` recovery (shared helper); plain built-in reverse unchanged.
- `inbound_translate.py` / `apply_inbound_events.py` / `inbound_differ.py` — use shared helper (retire `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`).
- `applier.py` — re-export shared helper in `__all__`.
- `mapping_config.py` — **add NEW** `declared_status_names(config)`: every Jira status NAME declared across config (`status_map` values ∪ `statuses`), for fetcher/preflight tolerated sets.
- `fetcher.py` — widen `_known_jira_statuses` to built-in ∪ config-declared names.
- `reconcile_helpers.py` — widen `preflight_status_mapping` tolerated set to include config-declared names (`repo_root` param).
- `reconcile.py` — thread `repo_root` into the `preflight_status_mapping` call.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit** — pure over the resolved map; tests hit REAL entry points
(`config.effective_status_map`, the outbound mappers, `_diff_status_annotation_labels`,
`inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields`, `fetcher._known_jira_statuses`,
`preflight_status_mapping`), never copies. Each AC names its test; alerts are non-fatal stderr
asserted via `capsys`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Effective forward map = `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>` via S1
  `resolve_for_project`; a non-default overlay changes the outbound target through the real
  mapper path — `test_status_config_effect`.
- [ ] An unmapped status **drifts**: the mutation omits `status` (Jira unchanged) + a non-fatal
  warning; never skipped nor a failure — `test_unmapped_status_drifts`.
- [ ] A config remap AND a collapsed pair (OTHER than blocked/cancelled) round-trip losslessly
  via `rebar-status:<local>` labels, recovered inbound without a reverse map —
  `test_status_remap_roundtrip`/`test_status_collapse_roundtrip`.
- [ ] A config-only/remapped Jira status name is tolerated by BOTH the fetcher known-set AND the
  post-mapper `preflight_status_mapping` (no spurious warning) —
  `test_fetcher_known_includes_config`, `test_preflight_tolerates_config_remap`.
- [ ] The duplicated `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` literal is retired: each inbound entry point
  (`inbound_fields`/`inbound_translate`/`apply_inbound_events`/`inbound_differ`) recovers a
  generalised label (local OTHER than blocked/cancelled) via the shared helper —
  `test_status_label_helper_single_source`.
- [ ] `value_maps`↔`config` parity tests in `state/test_config.py` stay green.
